entities.summary: The Good Parliament is the name traditionally given to the English Parliament of 1376. Sitting in Westminster from April 28 to July 10, it was the longest Parliament up until that time. It turned into a parliamentary revolution, with the Commons venting their grievances at decades of crippling taxation, misgovernment, and suspected endemic corruption among the ruling classes.
